source_artifacts.locator: approval card (as shown to the clerk)

capabilities.target: vendor master record including bank details
vendor bank account details in ERP vendor master

inputs.source: Supplier invoice uploaded to the supplier portal (externally authored document)

instructions.note: Agent is instructed to update vendor bank details whenever the invoice shows new bank details, with no requirement to verify the change against an independent trusted source before applying it.

The only stated safeguard before an irreversible payment or bank change is a prompt-directed request for a one-line approval summary; the prompt does not require the summary to disclose that bank details changed.

controls.name: Clerk approval card before payment or bank change
controls.decay_rationale: The gate is enforced outside the model (a human must click Approve), but the approver sees only a model-authored one-line summary rather than the raw bank-detail diff, so a more persuasive or selectively incomplete model summary (ASI09) defeats it; ~150 approvals/day compounds this through approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403).

controls.name: Bank-destination confirmation bound to the vendor system of record
controls.decay_rationale: An out-of-band confirmation of new bank details (e.g., callback to the phone number already on file) draws the destination from the system of record, not from model output, so it does not decay with model capability.

controls.name: Raw-action approval card showing bank-detail diff and full payment details
controls.decay_rationale: Showing the approver the actual ERP record diff (old/new bank account, change timestamp, amount, payee) instead of a model summary removes the model from the trust path for the approval decision.

findings.title: Summary-gated irreversible action (TC9): untrusted invoice drives bank-detail change and payment, visible to the clerk only as a one-line summary

attack_path.note: Untrusted supplier-uploaded invoice claims new bank details
Agent reads current vendor master/bank details to match the invoice
Agent updates vendor bank details based on invoice content per prompt.md:2, with no independent verification
Agent schedules payment to the now attacker-controlled bank account
Sole safeguard; approver sees only a one-line model summary, not the bank account numbers or change history

forecast.watch_signal: Model/version field in the platform config changing without a separate review (subject.model.swappable=true); approval throughput staying near 150/day with a near-100% approve rate; any incident where the summary omitted a bank-detail change.

evidence.observation: Agent updates vendor bank details directly from invoice content with no independent verification step.
The only safeguard before payment or bank change is a model-generated one-line approval summary.
Card shows only 'Pay Northwind Supplies $4,200.00 for INV-1187 (matches PO-5521)' with no bank account number and no indication that bank details were changed.
Bank account numbers and change history are explicitly not shown to the clerk; the gate is scored as approval_review_mode: model_summary.
Clerk approves roughly 150 cards per day, consistent with approval fatigue (SAFE-T1403).
ERP credential can update any vendor and schedule any payment (credential_scope: broad), so there is no least-privilege containment on the sink.
Model is upgraded with the platform with no separate review, which is the model_upgrade forecast trigger that defeats partially_dependent, model-summary approval gates.

recommendations.action: Change the approval card to a raw_action review: show masked bank account (old vs new, last 4 digits), payee, amount, and a flag whenever bank details changed this cycle, sourced directly from the ERP record rather than a model-written summary.
Require out-of-band verification of any new bank details (e.g., callback to the phone number already on file) before erp.update_vendor_bank_details takes effect, independent of invoice content.
Scope the ERP credential to least privilege and require a separately scoped second approver specifically for bank-detail changes, distinct from payment-amount approval.
Log and alert whenever a bank-detail change is followed by a payment within the same review cycle, and monitor per-clerk approval rate and daily volume for approval-fatigue signals.
Treat any model upgrade as a significant change (ISO 42001 8.2) requiring reassessment before deployment, since the approval gate is partially_dependent on model behavior.

rating.rationale: A single toxic chain drives the rating: an untrusted, supplier-authored invoice (source U) can drive a bank-detail change and payment scheduling (sink S3: irreversible spend, broad credential scope), giving inherent risk critical. The only control is a human approval gate; because the clerk reviews a model-written summary rather than the raw action (approval_review_mode: model_summary) and approves ~150 cards/day, rubric section 5 step 2 applies its moderate floor rather than a full severance, giving residual risk moderate. Because the underlying model is upgraded with the platform without separate review (model_upgrade trigger, subject.model.swappable=true), this partially_dependent gate is expected to fail first -- a stronger model produces more persuasive or selectively incomplete summaries (ASI09) -- collapsing the projected risk back to critical. No structural control (destination confirmation, credential scoping, raw-action review) currently severs or robustly contains the path; both are listed as missing_recommended.

limitations: This assessment reflects declared design and configuration as described in the provided artifacts (prompt.md, the approval card, and runtime notes), not observed runtime behavior.

No MCP/tool manifest or IaC was provided; capability fields such as credential_scope and is_egress are inferred from the runtime notes and prompt text, which limits confidence on exact system boundaries.
Autonomy step and runtime limits (max_unattended_steps, max_runtime_minutes) were not disclosed and are recorded as null rather than confirmed absent.
